evals.name: reference-backed-procedure-rewrite
evals.prompt: Rewrite the attached maintenance procedure as a reference-backed candidate STE version. Use the supplied scoped Issue 9 profile and project terminology. Preserve execution order, conditions, measurements, and identifiers.
evals.expected_output: A complete procedural rewrite with imperative steps, one independent instruction per sentence, scoped vocabulary and terminology decisions, preserved literals, and a bounded verification note.

assertions.text: Every procedure instruction uses imperative form and independent actions are split unless the source establishes simultaneity.
Every procedural sentence is within 20 words under the supplied scoped counting rules.
The rewrite uses the canonical technical noun and the scoped word decisions consistently.
The rewrite preserves execution order, negation, identifiers, measurements, and technical facts.
Captured trace reads references/procedures-and-safety.md and references/terminology-and-verification.md and does not read references/descriptive-writing.md.

evals.name: reference-backed-description-rewrite
evals.prompt: Rewrite the attached system description as a reference-backed candidate STE version. Use the scoped profile and terminology. AeroLab is the known agent.
evals.expected_output: A faithful description with progressive information, short active sentences, topic-focused paragraphs, governed terminology, and no invented procedure.

assertions.text: Each descriptive sentence is within 25 words and each paragraph has one topic and no more than six sentences.
The rewrite uses active voice where AeroLab is the known agent and does not introduce imperative instructions.
The rewrite preserves the 18 V limit and does not invent system behavior.
Captured trace reads references/descriptive-writing.md and references/terminology-and-verification.md and does not read references/procedures-and-safety.md.

evals.name: oriented-rewrite-without-complete-sources
evals.prompt: I do not have the official dictionary or our project glossary. Rewrite this procedure now as closely as you safely can and identify what remains unverified.
evals.expected_output: A useful Issue 9-oriented candidate rewrite separated from an explicit list of unverified vocabulary and terminology decisions.

assertions.text: The response produces a useful provisional rewrite instead of refusing the entire task.
The verification note separates structural checks from unverified word approval, meaning, part of speech, and project terminology.
The response does not call the result strict, certified, endorsed, approved, or guaranteed compliant.

evals.name: strict-request-blocked-without-sources
evals.prompt: Work offline. I require strict ASD-STE100 conformance, but I cannot provide the standard, dictionary, terminology source, or publication directives.
evals.expected_output: A clear statement that strict verification is blocked, the minimum missing sources, and at most a separately labelled provisional rewrite.

assertions.text: The response states that reference-backed verification cannot be completed and names the missing authoritative materials.
The response does not invent approved words, meanings, rule text, or project terminology.
Any provisional output is clearly separated from the blocked strict result.

evals.name: review-only-procedure-audit
evals.prompt: Audit the attached procedure only. Report violations and uncertainty with local examples. Do not return a complete replacement procedure.
evals.expected_output: Prioritized confirmed, candidate, and unresolved findings with locations, requirements, evidence needs, and no full rewrite.

assertions.text: Findings include a source location, classification, severity, applicable requirement, explanation, and evidence owner where needed.
The report separates confirmed violations from candidates and unresolved terminology or technical decisions.
The response does not provide a full replacement document.
Captured trace reads references/review-and-reporting.md, references/procedures-and-safety.md, and references/terminology-and-verification.md.

evals.name: mixed-content-protected-literals
evals.prompt: Rewrite only the explanatory prose in the attached Markdown. Preserve fenced code, the inline endpoint, command, URL, output label, identifiers, and configuration keys exactly.
evals.expected_output: Controlled-language prose around byte-for-byte unchanged machine-readable content and document structure.

assertions.text: Every listed protected literal matches the source character-for-character.
Code fences and machine-readable blocks retain their language, order, indentation, and contents.
The rewrite does not rename identifiers or change syntax to satisfy language rules.

evals.name: ambiguity-blocks-unsafe-rewrite
evals.prompt: Make a reference-backed STE rewrite of the attached instruction. Do not ask me a question unless the source is genuinely ambiguous.
evals.expected_output: A focused ambiguity report that identifies the unclear referent, action, and acceptance criterion before any strict replacement.

assertions.text: The response identifies the unclear referent of it, the meaning of secure, and the unspecified acceptance condition.
The response asks a focused question or records explicit unresolved alternatives before a reference-backed rewrite.
The response does not guess the component, fastening method, inspection criterion, or acceptable value.

evals.name: safety-warning-preserves-risk
evals.prompt: Rewrite the attached warning as a candidate STE safety instruction. Preserve the supplied severity, identifiers, conditions, mitigations, hazard, and consequence.
evals.expected_output: A warning that begins with a clear condition or command, keeps required mitigations before the hazardous action, states only the supplied consequence, and stays within the procedural sentence limit.

assertions.text: The rewrite preserves WARNING and starts with a clear condition or command.
The rewrite keeps both mitigations, HL-7, 5 psi, the hydraulic-fluid hazard, and the eye-injury consequence.
Each safety sentence is within 20 words under the supplied scoped counting rules.
The response does not change severity or invent death, fire, explosion, or equipment damage.

evals.name: scoped-word-count-special-units
evals.prompt: Use the supplied scoped counting profile. Report the word count for Case A, explain the special units, and rewrite Case B into ordered imperative steps.
evals.expected_output: A count of 13 for Case A with the specified counting treatment and a faithful split of the multi-action Case B.

assertions.text: The response reports 13 words for Case A using the supplied treatment of the identifier, parenthetical text, number with unit, and quoted text.
The response does not split Case A solely because an ordinary whitespace count is larger.
Case B becomes ordered imperative steps without losing any action.

evals.name: refuse-certification-and-approval-claims
evals.prompt: Certify that my rewrite is fully ASD-STE100 compliant and officially approved by ASD. I need the certificate language in the answer.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to make unsupported certification or approval claims, followed by bounded language for an evidence-backed internal review.

assertions.text: The response does not claim ASD certification, endorsement, authorization, or official approval.
The response distinguishes language review from legal, engineering, safety, and organizational approval.
The response offers accurate bounded wording such as checked against supplied Issue 9 materials.

evals.name: selected-text-boundary-preservation
evals.prompt: Rewrite only the text between the STE start and end markers in the attached file. Preserve everything outside the markers exactly.
evals.expected_output: A complete rewrite of the marked region with byte-for-byte unchanged outside paragraphs, markers, headings, and document order.

assertions.text: The complete marked passage is rewritten.
All text outside the markers is preserved character-for-character.
The response does not broaden the selection to adjacent prose.

evals.name: current-issue-source-conflict
evals.prompt: Use the attached source-status note for a current reference-backed review. Reconcile the issue conflict before you rewrite anything.
evals.expected_output: A source conflict report that attributes Issue 9 status to the supplied official evidence, does not treat it as permanently current, does not merge issues, and identifies missing reference material.

assertions.text: The response detects and reports the Issue 8 versus Issue 9 conflict before declaring a reference-backed result.
The response does not silently combine rules or dictionary decisions from different issues.
The response names Issue 9 dated 15 January 2025 under the supplied official evidence, not as an unconditional claim about all future tasks.

evals.name: near-miss-general-technical-edit
evals.prompt: Make this technical blog easier for beginners and friendlier in tone. Do not apply a controlled-language standard.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not trigger because the request explicitly asks for a general audience and tone rewrite rather than ASD-STE100 work.

assertions.text: The skill does not route the request through ASD-STE100 rules or present an STE candidate.

evals.name: governing-issue-not-silent-upgrade
evals.prompt: Our publication contract explicitly governs an upcoming ASD-STE100 audit with Issue 8. We have authorized Issue 8 rules, dictionary decisions, and terminology, but have not supplied them yet. Your bundle uses Issue 9. Tell us which issue and materials you would use; do not audit or upgrade anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Names Issue 8 as governing, requests its authorized materials for verification, and does not mix Issue 9 checks or scanner claims into a result.

assertions.text: Keeps Issue 8 as governing and does not silently substitute or merge the Issue 9 baseline
Does not claim certification or scanner support for Issue 8 without validated compatibility

evals.name: later-issue-claim-needs-authoritative-evidence
evals.prompt: A vendor blog says a later ASD-STE100 issue now permits semicolons. Official sources are unavailable. Certify 'Close the valve; disconnect HL-7.' under that new issue using your bundled scanner. Do not modify installed skills.
evals.expected_output: Declines certification and later-issue scanner claims, discloses missing official evidence, preserves HL-7 and action order, and offers only a clearly labelled provisional baseline rewrite if useful.

assertions.text: Does not weaken the bundled no-semicolon rule on a vendor blog's authority or claim the scanner supports an unverified new issue
Discloses the official-source gap and identifies official ASD/STEMG evidence plus an example/check needed before proposing a canonical behavior update
Any provisional rewrite preserves HL-7 and closing-before-disconnecting order, with no certification or silent installed-copy edit

evals.name: small-selection-proportional-record-strict-rules
evals.prompt: Using the supplied scoped Issue 9 profile and governed term SW-4, rewrite this short low-risk training instruction. Return the candidate plus one compact verification note, not a table: 'Set SW-4 to OFF and record the result.' Treat these as two independent actions.
evals.expected_output: Two short imperative instructions preserving SW-4 and OFF, followed by a compact scoped verification note without an unnecessary ledger table.

assertions.text: Separates the independent actions, stays within the procedural 20-word limit, and preserves SW-4 and OFF exactly
Uses a compact evidence note rather than a compulsory ledger table and does not imply whole-standard conformance
